## Two observations for the planner (scope-sharpening, Goal unchanged)

- **The check is branch-AGNOSTIC, which makes it strictly simpler and stronger than the
  body sketches.** An unresolvable import is a latent `ModuleNotFoundError` wherever it
  sits — production branch, smoke branch, or nested three helpers deep — because
  resolvability does not depend on reachability. So this check needs no smoke/production
  branch analysis at all, and thereby inherits NONE of the
  `--check-smoke-blind-spots` scanner's documented false negatives (one-level helper
  resolution, un-recursed `ast.Match` bodies, dynamic dispatch, non-`smoke`-named flags).
  A plain `ast.walk` satisfies acceptance criterion 2 (the #1336 nested-helper shape) for
  free. The only legitimate exemption is an import deliberately guarded by
  `try/except ImportError` on a non-load-bearing path.
- **`importlib.metadata.packages_distributions()` resolves all 6 measured
  import-name != dist-name cases with zero hand-maintenance** (PIL->pillow,
  dotenv->python-dotenv, hydra->hydra-core, sklearn->scikit-learn, umap->umap-learn,
  yaml->pyyaml). But it reads the LIVE venv, so a lint keyed on it is
  environment-dependent and would give different verdicts on a fresh pod. The body
  requires a table-driven, unit-tested mapping. Recommend the planner weigh a hybrid:
  static table as the deterministic primary, venv metadata as an optional cross-check that
  flags table drift, and a loud FAIL on any unmapped unknown (as the body specifies).

## Finding 2 [Methodology lens] — the overlay leg reds every worktree (more severe than reported)

**VERIFIED, and worse than the critic stated.** `external/open-instruct` is a git GITLINK, not a tree:

- `git ls-tree HEAD external/` returns `160000 commit 45901fd0...` for `open-instruct`, while all three siblings (`agentic-backdoor`, `jacobian-lens`, `training-against-misalignment`) are `040000 tree`.
- Main checkout HAS `external/open-instruct/open_instruct`.
- All 4 probed worktrees (issue-2388 / 2241 / 2428 / 2246) have the pkgdir ABSENT while `scripts/train_stage_dpo.py` — the file carrying the 7 `open_instruct` import sites — is PRESENT.

So the plan's §4.1 step 5 rule ("absent overlay dir → FAIL naming the missing overlay") fires on 7 sites in EVERY worktree. Since Step 9c tests run in the issue worktree, that reds #2253's own gate; and if acceptance is instead run at the main checkout and lands green, it reds every future issue touching `workflow_lint.py` — the exact #1388 fleet-wide wedge the plan's §0.0 and §11 D1 call non-negotiable. The behavior is pinned by the plan's own `test_live_tree_full_run_is_clean` + `test_overlay_dir_absent_fails`, so it is not implementer-recoverable inside the plan's allowed deviations.

**The escalation the critic missed: `.gitmodules` is EMPTY.** The gitlink is orphaned — no submodule URL is registered anywhere — so `git submodule update --init` cannot materialize it, and a `tests/sparse_cones.txt` entry structurally cannot either (a sparse cone only materializes parent-repo content, and a gitlink is not parent-repo content). There is no repair path that makes the pkgdir appear in a worktree. Any fix must therefore make overlay resolution independent of the pkgdir existing on disk — e.g. resolve when the overlay path is a tracked gitlink/tree at HEAD — rather than trying to get the directory populated.

## Five Must-Fix items (every one orchestrator-verified against the live repo)

1. **The overlay rule is wrong in BOTH directions — delete it, waive per-site.** Converged from
   Methodology-Claude and Alternatives-Codex independently. (A) `external/open-instruct` is a git
   GITLINK (`160000 commit`, unlike its three `040000 tree` siblings) and `.gitmodules` is EMPTY,
   so the package dir is absent in every worktree (4 probed: issue-2388/2241/2428/2246) while
   `scripts/train_stage_dpo.py` is present — the plan's "absent overlay dir → FAIL" rule reds the
   bundled run and the live-tree pin in every worktree, including this task's own Step 9c gate
   (#1388 fleet wedge). No repair path exists: an orphaned gitlink cannot be materialized by
   `submodule update --init`, and a sparse cone cannot materialize non-parent-repo content.
   (B) Presence does not prove importability anyway: `find_spec('open_instruct')` from the repo
   root is None, `open-instruct` is absent from `pyproject.toml`, and `launch_stage.py:477`
   (`cwd = str(OI_DIR) if backend == "open_instruct" else None`) gives the `midtrain` backend that
   launches `train_stage_dpo.py` (`:285`) a repo-root CWD. So `OVERLAY_IMPORT_ROOTS` is
   functionally a hidden allowlist — the live-tree test would go green precisely BECAUSE the table
   suppresses all 7 sites — contradicting acceptance criterion A3 and masking an apparent real
   latent defect. FIX: delete the table + its pin test, waive the 7 sites per-site with reasons
   naming the unproven launcher CWD/PYTHONPATH contract. Worktree-invariant, honest under A3, less
   code. **NOTE: this supersedes an earlier orchestrator-drafted fix ("resolve on a tracked
   gitlink at HEAD"), which would have made direction (B) strictly worse.**
2. **Dist-universe over-acceptance: extras are never synced.** `umap-learn` is only in the `viz`
   extra (`pyproject.toml:66-67`); the pod bootstrap runs a bare `uv sync --locked`
   (`bootstrap_pod.sh:425`); a repo-wide sweep finds ZERO real `--extra`/`--all-extras` uses. With
   `IMPORT_TO_DIST` mapping `umap → umap-learn`, all four bare in-function `import umap` sites
   read RESOLVED while a fresh pod raises ModuleNotFoundError. Blast radius is exactly one root —
   every `flash_attn`/`liger_kernel` site (9 checked) is already `try/except`-guarded. FIX (the
   orchestrator's scope call, recorded): keep the wide universe as the FAIL boundary — the Goal
   pins the oracle to "resolvable from uv.lock/pyproject.toml", so narrowing it would contradict
   the Goal — and add a WARN tier naming the extra, plus a docstring "PASS ≠ installed-by-default"
   caveat. Two of the four umap sites are DELIBERATE lazy imports (one carries a comment saying
   so), which is what tipped this away from forcing four waivers. Correct §0.0, whose "would have
   killed a pod run after uv sync" claim is what actually over-reaches.
3. **`if TYPE_CHECKING:` imports fire on healthy code** (Codex methodology; Claude methodology
   raised it as a concern). Branch-agnostic `ast.walk` scans imports that can never execute, so an
   unlocked type-only dep FAILs on healthy code. Zero instances today — latent, not live. FIX:
   exclude canonical TYPE_CHECKING guard bodies; keep smoke branches and ordinary conditionals;
   restate the §1 "strict superset" claim accurately rather than deleting it.
4. **The `try` exemption exempts positions the handler does not protect** (both Codex twins,
   independently). §4.1 exempts body, handler AND orelse. But an exception raised in a `handler`
   suite is not caught by that same `try`; nor is one in `orelse`; nor is an import inside a
   function DEFINED in the try body (deferred execution). All three shapes PASS the lint and still
   raise ModuleNotFoundError — the motivating failure class. Correct Python semantics; the
   predicate is simply wrong. FIX: exempt only `try.body`, stopping at FunctionDef/AsyncFunctionDef/
   Lambda boundaries; parameterize tests so handler/orelse/deferred-body all FAIL.
5. **Per-`(file, root)` waiver absorption is verdict-corrupting** (both Codex twins). "A waiver on
   any one site of the pair exempts the pair" lets an old optional-use waiver silently exempt a
   later LOAD-BEARING import of the same root in the same file, with no adjacent declaration and no
   review signal — certifying exactly the class the check exists to stop. FIX: apply waivers per
   AST import site, then dedup only the REMAINING errors.
